value.title: The open project clock confirms complete synchronization of that project
value.statement: Full-clock persistence is attempted by canonical workspace path only after required project accounts, child jobs, ready local changes and cleanup succeed in one run. Wrong-account, track-only, layer-only and cancelled passes cannot certify full completion. Fast outbound uploads are independent of account schedules and never write full completion clocks. Separate feature and attachment Save flags exclude all corresponding queued edits until Save; after-commit events retain their owning map. Successful project/account recovery ACK is persisted before final workspace cleanup and full-clock commit; an empty recovery queue alone cannot certify full completion. Recovery target UID/path/mapName, canonical-path clock and path-partitioned import journal are separate saved-state keys. Their relocation or identity changes require an explicit migration/invalidation contract. Post-ACK cleanup failure does not re-enqueue completed pairs; startup journal recovery reads retained pairs, not old clocks. Request dispatch, next schedule and SYNC_FINISH are not full completion ACKs. Known source limitation under AUDIT-TODO-SYNC-ACK-RECOVERY: SharedPreferences commit false can leave a new cached clock or queue value while disk differs; durable state needs an independent disk/restart oracle. The required durable-clock invariant is not proven by a same-process getter and these fault branches are NOT_RUN. Journal APIs shield the accepted seven-key typed/presence cohort per exact preferences owner before writing; false or thrown writes preserve the prior process view, and later ordinary writes stage all known keys without clearing unknown keys. Only true advances that view. Initial raw bootstrap has unknown disk provenance; no compensating write, restart rollback or resend policy follows from this source fix.
